Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law · Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

sword noun

also swords, toy sword, wooden sword, saber, sabre

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.62
Liv. 5.48.9
Caes. BC 3.93: gladiōs strīnxērunt (Lewis & Short)

gladius, gladiī m.

noun, second declension

To draw a sword, gladium stringere (Cic. Phil. 2.21, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ēnsis, ēnsis m. — sword

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Verg. A. 2.393 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 7.10.9 (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Ov.)

    Almost only in the poets (Lewis & Short).

  • rudis, rudis f. — a wooden practice sword, a foil; a toy sword

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Suet. Cal. 32 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Phil. 2.74 (Lewis & Short)

    The staff with which soldiers and gladiators practised; a gladiator was given one on his discharge (Lewis & Short). Its use for a child’s wooden sword is ours.

Examples

  • fulgentem gladium ē lacūnārī saetā equīnā aptum dēmittī jussit

    he had a gleaming sword let down from the ceiling, hanging by a single horsehairCic. Tusc. 5.62

  • additus ab īnsolente Gallō ponderī gladius, audītaque intoleranda Rōmānīs vōx, Vae victīs

    the arrogant Gaul threw his sword on the weights too, and the Romans heard words they could not bear: ‘Woe to the beaten!’Liv. 5.48.9

  • Gladium stringe!

    Draw your sword!composed

  • ēnsis falcātus

    a saberTraupman 373

See also weapon, shield, helmet, knife.
